title: No Verified Case Supplied: Evidence Must Lead Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: No arrest, seizure, verdict, or Vietnamese health alert appears in supplied material. SDE must demand abolition without inventing victims or incidents.
body_html:
No police seizure, court verdict, intercepted shipment, or named Vietnamese health alert appears in the material supplied for this dispatch. That gap matters. Stolen companion animals deserve truth, not invented scenes; public-health demands deserve evidence, not inflated claims.

Facts Before Fury

The supplied report contains investigation targets and source lists, but no completed finding with an article title, date, agency, defendant, case number, quantity, quotation, or canonical URL. Claims about stun guns, poison bait, wire nooses, forged quarantine documents, packed cages, and cross-provincial transport therefore cannot be presented as documented events here.

Rabies remains a severe public-health threat. Transmission generally requires infected saliva to enter through a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis, including vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. World Health Organization rabies guidance explains these risks.

Demand Proof. Demand Protection.

Household exposure incidents and commercial animal-trade controls are separate dimensions of biosecurity. Neither should be linked without primary evidence. Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, journalists, and local authorities need transparent records: arrests, seizures, veterinary documents, court outcomes, and public-health notices.

SDE's policy demand remains clear: nationwide abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030, stronger enforcement against theft and illegal transport, and effective veterinary controls during the transition. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
